nary_nodes.label: UIBC names Castel World Confectioner
evidence: The International Union of Bakers and Confectioners (UIBC) named him World Confectioner of the Year last month.
Castel received the UIBC award presented annually to a leading figure in the profession in recognition of their career and contribution to the trade on July 14 in Singapore.

nary_nodes.label: Castel tests new recipes
evidence: The smell of warm bread hangs in the air at one of Benoît Castel's patisseries in Paris, where the newly crowned world's best pastry chef was hard at work testing new recipes.

His fingers covered in cookie dough, the 54-year-old with salt-and-pepper hair had returned to his usual routine as an "artisan-retailer" after the International Union of Bakers and Confectioners (UIBC) named him World Confectioner of the Year last month.

nary_nodes.label: Métayer crowned champion
evidence: Three years after fellow French pastry chef Nina Métayer was crowned champion, Castel received the UIBC award presented annually to a leading figure in the profession in recognition of their career and contribution to the trade on July 14 in Singapore.

nary_nodes.label: Castel set out on his own
evidence: When Castel set out on his own in 2012 after working with chef Hélène Darroze, at the prestigious Hotel Costes and La Grande Epicerie de Paris, he discovered the art of breadmaking.

nary_nodes.label: New venue opens in September
evidence: Alongside his daughter Margot, he is set to open a new venue in Paris in September – a cross between a café, a restaurant and a bakery-patisserie.

nary_nodes.label: Mission to be world champion daily
evidence: "I have a mission: to be the world champion every day in my shop for my customers," he said, eyes twinkling.

nary_nodes.label: It's all about the product
evidence: At the helm of several establishments in Paris, Castel has never strayed from his motto: "It's all about the product."

nary_nodes.label: Work is no trivial matter
evidence: "Our work is no trivial matter, every day we make things that people put into their bodies," said Castel, who hails from Brittany in western France.

nary_nodes.label: Best-seller is chocolate choux
evidence: The pastry shop's glass cases are arrayed with blueberry and raspberry tartlets, cherry clafoutis and vanilla flans, but his best-seller is a chocolate choux pastry.
"If we stopped making it, there'd be protests," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Product dictates recipe
evidence: "The funny thing with this profession is that it's the product that dictates the recipe," he said enthusiastically from his kitchen, which opens onto the shop and the dining room, a popular spot for brunch.

nary_nodes.label: Castel is demanding perfectionist
evidence: The pastry chef is "demanding, he has this slightly perfectionist side we're very fond of", said Montbabut, who has been working with him for six years.
"He's there alongside his workers every day and loves to pass things on," he added.

nary_nodes.label: Artists push new ideas
evidence: Always in search of new inspiration, Castel also collaborates with artists to create Yule logs. "Because they're not technically limited in their ideas, it pushes us to try new things," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Cook, gardener, baker, pastry chef
evidence: "These days, I'm as much a cook, a gardener and a baker as I am a pastry chef," he said.
"But above all else, I'm a pastry chef."
